title: Lamb of God, Who Bear'st Away
description: Lamb of God, Who Bear'st Away in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 463. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lamb of God, who bear'st a-way All the sins of all man-kind, Bow a na-tion to thy sway; While we may ac-cep-tance find, Let us thank-ful-ly em-brace The last of-fers of thy grace.

lines: Lamb of God, who bear'st away
All the sins of all mankind,
Bow a nation to thy sway;
The last offers of thy grace.
Feel our sins by grace forgiven,
Find in thee the way to heaven.
Tell them, "I have died for you!"
Sink the mountain to a plain;
Bring the pride of sinners down;
Melt the rebels with thy blood!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
